title: set_reports block in analysis_result.json embeds name/title/notes/note without escaping, and set peaks inherit a sticky std::fixed
mechanism: `extra << "\n    {\"name\": \"" << sr.name << "\"" ... << ", \"title\": \"" << sr.title << "\""` (806-809), `extra << "\"" << sr.notes[j] << "\""` (823), `", \"note\": \"" << f.note << "\""` (838). Notes include user text such as `"이름 패턴 '" + pat + "' 에 맞는 파트 없음"` (UnifiedAnalyzer.cpp:1157) and renderer error strings (UnifiedAnalyzerSectionRender.cpp:299). metrics.json (unified_analyzer.cpp:362-432) escapes the same strings with jesc; this block does not. Also, `std::setprecision(8)` at 832 inherits std::fixed only when motion/quality/beam sections were non-empty, so set peak formatting depends on unrelated sections.
scenario: Reproduced: title `Front\Metal "A"` (the SetReportSpec comment's own pattern example `Front\\Metal`) makes toExtendedJSON emit `"title": "Front\Metal "A""`, and json.loads raises 'Invalid \escape'. A *SET_PART_LIST_TITLE title containing a quote or backslash, or an unmatched YAML part_patterns entry containing a backslash, breaks the custom-report run's analysis_result.json.
consumers: The custom_report/<run>/analysis_result.json written by koo_custom_report runs. The Python custom/sphere/impact report code reads set_reports/<set>/metrics.json, not this file, so no current Python consumer breaks. The defect is latent for any tool that reads analysis_result.json from that folder.
suggested_fix: Use escapeJSON/jesc for every string in toExtendedJSON (set_reports name/title/notes/note, surface_strain description/note, motion/element_quality part_name) and jnum for the peak values.

title: beam_analysis and motion_analysis JSON summaries use fixed(6): peak times 1.5e-7 and 1.4e-7 both print as 0.000000, and small SI displacements/velocities print as 0
mechanism: beam: `<< ", \"peak_max\": " << std::fixed << std::setprecision(6) << gmax << ", \"peak_max_time\": " << t_max` (791-796). motion: `<< ", \"peak_velocity\": " << std::fixed << std::setprecision(6) << m.peak_velocity_magnitude << ", \"peak_acceleration\": " ... << ", \"max_displacement\": "` (724-726). BeamAnalyzer.cpp:122-129 leaves tp.max_value/min_value at 0.0 when every beam value in a state is non-finite (deleted), so peak_max can report a placeholder 0 for compression-only beams.
scenario: Reproduced: beam points at t=1.5e-7 (max 12.0) and t=1.4e-7 give `peak_max_time 0.0`. A motion point with avg velocity 4e-7 and max displacement 3e-7 (SI m/s, m) gives peak_velocity 0.0 and max_displacement 0.0.
consumers: No Python consumer reads beam_analysis or motion_analysis from JSON (the deep/sphere/impact reports use motion CSVs, and beam output is unused), so the defect is latent.
suggested_fix: Use jnum() for these fields and add a per-state validity count for beam points instead of 0.

title: Stress histories are serialized with a hard-coded unit "MPa" regardless of deck units
mechanism: `stress_results_[i].unit = "MPa";` (409), also max_principal (421) and min_principal (426). partStatsToJSON writes it as-is: `oss << ind2 << "\"unit\": \"" << stats.unit` (AnalysisResult.hpp:508).
scenario: Real Test_Impact_A (a GPa-mm-ms deck): analysis_result.json stress_history[0] has unit "MPa" with global_max 0.08627328, which is actually 86 MPa. A Pa deck would carry 3e8 labeled MPa.
consumers: koo_impact_report/loader.py:1234 copies it into rec["stress_unit"] (not currently displayed, since the impact report uses _detect_unit_system). The deep report hard-codes 'MPa' in its HTML independently. Any external reader of analysis_result.json (the DynaForge export) would mislabel.
suggested_fix: Emit an empty unit or "deck_units" unless the unit system is actually detected (for example from the keyword file's *CONTROL_UNITS or the impact loader's detector).

title: max_element_id/min_element_id written as 0 for series that never set them
mechanism: timePointToJSON always writes `"max_element_id": tp.max_element_id, "min_element_id": tp.min_element_id` (491-492). SinglePassAnalyzer never sets min_element_id for eff_plastic_strain, vm_strain, σ1 or ε1 series, or max_element_id for σ3/ε3 series (SinglePassAnalyzer.cpp 771-797, 812-826). The default 0 goes out as an element ID.
scenario: Real Test_Impact_A stress/part_10_max_principal_stress.csv rows are `0.000001,0.040159,0.031681,0.035920,34004,0`, and the JSON has min_element_id 0 at every point of max_principal_history. 0 is not a valid LS-DYNA element ID.
consumers: No current Python consumer reads min_element_id (the sphere loader reads only Max_Element_ID; deep report peak_element_id uses the stress series' max_element_id), so the defect is latent.
suggested_fix: Track and write the IDs, or omit the key (or write null) for series where it is not tracked.

title: Max_Disp_Node_ID is internal 1-based node index, not the user node ID
mechanism: `max_node_id = static_cast<int32_t>(node_idx + 1);  // 1-based` is written to the 'Max_Disp_Node_ID' CSV column (unified_analyzer.cpp:93). mesh.real_node_ids exists but is not used.
scenario: /data/ball_drop_test_v7/ex01 deck node IDs are 1..338 and then jump to 1001. The CSV reports Max_Disp_Node_ID 1427 and 1317, which are actually real nodes 2089 and 1979. Nodes 1427 and 1317 also exist in the deck, so a user looking them up checks the wrong node.
consumers: motion/part_N_motion.csv (parsed into koo_deep_report MotionData.max_disp_node, documented as '최대 변위 노드 ID' in DATA_STRUCTURE.md). No report currently renders it.

title: Extended JSON set_reports writes notes/name/title unescaped; a multi-line ffmpeg error makes analysis_result.json invalid
mechanism: `extra << "\"" << sr.notes[j] << "\"";` (also sr.name at :806 and sr.title at :809, which comes from the *SET title). metrics.json escapes these via jesc, but analysis_result.json does not. UnifiedAnalyzerSectionRender.cpp:306 pushes `"뷰 실패 [..]: " + err`, where err comes from SectionViewRenderer::assembleMp4:2196 `"ffmpeg failed (exit " + rc + "): " + ffout`, which contains raw newlines.
scenario: A set view whose ffmpeg encode fails, for example an odd width that libx264 rejects, or 'sh: 1: ffmpeg: not found'. The note contains '\n', and Python json.load raises 'Invalid control character' (verified). Every consumer of that folder's analysis_result.json fails to load the run.
consumers: Anything reading analysis_result.json in a folder that also has set_reports (see the shared-folder custom report finding): sphere, impact reuse, deep _parse_outputs
suggested_fix: Route all string fields in toExtendedJSON (motion/quality part_name, set name/title/notes, surface description/note) through escapeJSON.

title: element_quality min_jacobian written fixed(4): small negative Jacobians print as '-0.0000' and fail the `< 0` critical check
mechanism: `<< std::fixed << std::setprecision(4) << q.peak_aspect_ratio ... << ", \"min_jacobian\": " << q.min_jacobian`. deep html_report.py:1970 `q.min_jacobian < 0 ? 'crit' : (q.min_jacobian < 0.3 ? 'warn' : '')`.
scenario: A barely inverted element with scaled Jacobian -4e-5 is written as '-0.0000', parsed as -0.0, and `-0 < 0` is false. The cell is styled 'warn' instead of 'crit' and shows '-0.000'.
suggested_fix: Use defaultfloat with setprecision(10) (the existing jnum helper) for the quality fields.

title: Time-series JSON (data points, global_max/min, time_of_max) uses fixed(8), so values below 5e-9 become 0
mechanism: timePointToJSON:485 `oss << std::fixed << std::setprecision(8)` and partStatsToJSON:512 `std::fixed << std::setprecision(8) << stats.globalMax()`. The file's own jnum comment (:692-697) documents this hazard for hotspot fields but not for histories. HEAD 63577f5 fixes it after 36ea5db.
scenario: Eff. plastic strain peak 3e-9 is written as 0.00000000, so strain_history global_max reads as 0 ('no plasticity'). Production Test_005 JSON strain entries are quantized to 1e-08 (e.g. min -1e-08).
suggested_fix: Serialize with jnum (defaultfloat, setprecision(10)), as HEAD already does.

title: Principal and strain CSVs carry element ID 0 as if real in one ID column
mechanism: For σ1 only `tp1.max_element_id` is set (:775). For σ3 only `tp3.min_element_id` is set (:784), and for ε_p/ε_vm/ε1/ε3 only one side is set. writePartCSV (:54-55) writes both Max_Element_ID and Min_Element_ID, so the unset side is printed as 0.
scenario: part_N_min_principal_stress.csv has Max_Element_ID=0 on every row, and the eff_plastic_strain CSV has Min_Element_ID=0. The sphere loader (loader.py:253-259) reads Max_Element_ID into max_element_ids for every series, so σ3 and ε3 series get all-zero element IDs.
consumers: CSV readers; koo_sphere_report TimeSeriesData.max_element_ids (currently rendered only for von Mises)
suggested_fix: Leave the unset ID column empty (as writeSurfaceStrainCSV does for missing tensors), or populate both IDs.

title: Requested motion part that is not in the mesh produces an all-zero motion time series instead of an error
mechanism: `active_parts_ = part_ids_;` does not check part_node_indices_. computeAverageDisplacement returns `Vec3(0, 0, 0)` and computeMaxDisplacement returns `{0.0, 0}` when `part_node_indices_.find(part_id) == end()`. The point is still pushed for every state and written to motion/part_<id>_motion.csv.
scenario: `koo_deep_report --parts 5,999`, or koo_impact_report run_analysis(part_ids=[impactor_part_id]) with an ID taken from a keyword file that is not in this d3plot (e.g. a stale .k in the directory), writes part_999_motion.csv with Avg_Disp/Vel/Acc and Max_Disp all 0.000000 for every state. The impactor trajectory then shows zero penetration and zero velocity.
consumers: motion/part_*_motion.csv → koo_impact_report _extract_trajectory (loader.py:1317-1350), koo_sphere_report _load_motion_csv, koo_deep_report motion parser.
suggested_fix: Drop parts with no nodes in initialize() and log them (or fail when nothing remains). Do not emit rows for them.

title: Motion velocity at the first state and acceleration at the first two states are written as 0 instead of 'not available'; recorded nodal velocities (IV) are ignored
mechanism: `if (state_count_ > 0 && dt > 0) { ...avg_velocity = disp_diff/dt }` and `if (state_count_ > 1 && dt > 0) { ...avg_acceleration... }`. Otherwise MotionTimePoint keeps its default {0,0,0} and the row is written to the CSV like any other value.
scenario: A drop run with *INITIAL_VELOCITY 5000 mm/s writes Avg_Vel_Mag=0.000000 at t=0 and Avg_Acc=0 at the first two states, even though d3plot IV=1 holds the true nodal velocity. koo_impact_report already has to work around 'the t=0 v=0 artefact' (loader.py:404-439); plots and any consumer taking vel[0] get 0.
consumers: motion CSV → koo_impact_report ImpactorTrajectory vel_x/y/z and ke[0], koo_deep_report/koo_sphere_report motion plots.
suggested_fix: Use state.node_velocities / node_accelerations when IV/IA > 0. Otherwise leave the first samples empty or NaN in the CSV instead of 0.

title: Max_Disp_Node_ID is the internal 1-based index, not the user node ID
mechanism: `max_node_id = static_cast<int32_t>(node_idx + 1);  // 1-based` never maps through mesh_.real_node_ids / mesh_.nodes[idx].id, which GeometryParser fills from NARBS.
scenario: A deck whose node IDs are not the identity (the comment at UnifiedAnalyzer.cpp:901-904 cites results/d3plot, where real_node_ids diverge from index 28293 onward to 29625..30955): a peak at internal index 29000 is reported as node 29001, but the user node is 30332.
suggested_fix: Report mesh_.nodes[node_idx].id (already the real ID when NARBS is present).

title: A family file that fails to open or parse silently truncates every later state; only stderr is warned
mechanism: Parallel path: `if (result.success) {...} else { std::cerr << "WARNING: Stopping at file_idx " ...; break; }` (l.305-313). The sequential path breaks the same way (l.104-109, 126-129). StateDataParser::parse_all also does `catch (const std::exception& e) { done = true; }`. The caller gets a shorter vector with no flag, and fillMetadata writes num_states/end_time from it.
scenario: If d3plot07 of a 20-file family hits an I/O error on NFS or a permission problem, states from d3plot07 onward are dropped. analysis_result.json reports num_states=N_truncated and end_time earlier than the real run, and peaks after that time are missing with no marker in any output.
consumers: Every unified_analyzer output (stress/strain/motion/surface/hotspot) and metadata.num_states/end_time → all Python reports.
suggested_fix: Propagate the failure: return an error, or record truncated=true, the failing file and the expected-vs-read state counts in metadata so reports can flag it.

title: Stress unit hard-coded as "MPa" regardless of deck units
mechanism: `stress_results_[i].unit = "MPa";` (also max/min principal at l.421, 426). partStatsToJSON writes it as "unit" and koo_deep_report copies it into the series (d3plot_reader.py:569, html_report.py:341).
scenario: A kg-mm-ms deck (stress in GPa, peak 0.0863) or an SI deck (Pa, peak 3e8) is labeled "unit": "MPa" in analysis_result.json, so 0.0863 reads as 0.0863 MPa.
suggested_fix: Leave unit empty or "deck" unless the unit system is known (e.g. from *CONTROL_UNITS or a config value).

title: Sticky std::fixed in toExtendedJSON: element-quality metrics at 4 decimals, surface-strain values at 8, beam peaks at 6
mechanism: `<< ", \"peak_aspect_ratio\": " << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4)` (l.741) stays in effect for min_jacobian, min/max_volume_change and the per-point jac_min/vol_min (l.758+ only reset precision, not the fixed format). Surface strain sets `std::fixed << std::setprecision(6)` (l.854) and then setprecision(8) for normal/e1/e3/evm/eff_plastic values (l.865-878). Beam peaks use `std::fixed << std::setprecision(6)` (l.791).
scenario: A scaled Jacobian of -0.00004 prints as "-0.0000", so an inverted element reads as zero. A surface strain of 3e-9 prints as 0.00000000. A beam moment of 4e-7 (kN·mm) prints as 0.000000.
consumers: analysis_result.json element_quality (koo_deep_report d3plot_reader.py:491-510), surface_strain_analysis and beam_analysis.
suggested_fix: Use std::defaultfloat with setprecision(10) (or std::scientific) for numeric fields, and reset format flags per section.
